title: Renaming a field/concept or dropping one on a live app with data
body: Never rename by deleting the old field and adding a new one with a different name -- that reads to the platform as an unrelated drop+add and either refuses (if the table has data) or destroys the old column's data. Instead: (1) Rename -- add `renamedFrom` to the field object (`{"name":"fullName","renamedFrom":"name",...}`) for a field rename, or to the concept object itself (`{"name":"Customer","renamedFrom":"Client",...}`) for a table rename. This applies in place on the next boot -- zero data loss, no acknowledgment needed. (2) New required field on a populated table -- declare a literal `default` (e.g. `"default": "pending"`) so it backfills automatically; a `defaultExpression`-only field or a required bond field is refused (bonds have no automatic backfill -- make it optional instead, or accept the destructive path). (3) Dropping a field/concept is genuinely destructive and needs authorization: run `Build-NpdevApp.ps1 -Upgrade -PlanOnly` first to see the itemized plan and the acknowledgment token, then re-run with `-AcknowledgeDestructive <token>` (or submit `{toFingerprint, ackToken}` to `POST /api/admin/schema-migration/acknowledge` on the CURRENTLY RUNNING app, SUPERUSER-gated, before deploying the new jar). A rename and an unrelated acknowledged drop on the SAME table both apply correctly in the same boot -- the rename never waits on or gets blocked by the drop. (4) The deprecated blanket posture (`schemaLifecycle.strategy: DropAndRecreateOnStructureChange` + `allowDestructiveRecreate: true`) pre-authorizes column drops and type narrowings without a token, but it does NOT authorize dropping a whole concept -- a table drop always requires the itemized token. Authorized destructive changes execute SURGICALLY (only the itemized tables/columns are touched); the whole-schema recreation happens only when the delta report contains an item the surgical path cannot explain. New app definitions should use `strategy: KeepExistingIfCompatible` + `allowDestructiveRecreate: false`, which makes the token the only route to destruction. See docs/SCHEMA_EVOLUTION.md for the full worked example.
